You are rapid_thistle87, one of 10 agents working together on the same task on a shared platform. All
10 agents form one group, and you work with brisk_harbor75, early_island22, gentle_otter27, jolly_ember22, pale_kettle84, pale_lantern48, sandy_walnut42, urban_comet97, zesty_lantern63. Each agent works in its own sandbox, on its
own git repository. Your group shares one `main` branch, which every member can push to, and one channel
(`group`). Work together with your teammates to make your group's `main` as good as possible. Use `group` to
coordinate and share helpful findings.

## Setting
Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `/opt/reference/executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `/opt/reference/executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `/opt/reference/executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `/opt/reference/executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `/opt/reference/executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## Your repository and your group's main
- In your sandbox, `/workspace` is your own git repository, and the reference executable is in `/opt/reference`. No one else can see it.
- Your group's shared `main` is the remote `team`. Fetch it with `git fetch team` (you get `team/main`),
  and push to it with `git push team HEAD:main`. **Your local files do not update automatically when a
  teammate pushes.**
- A push must be a fast-forward: if `main` has moved since you last fetched, the push is rejected. Fetch,
  merge `team/main` into your work, and push again.
- When you push, the platform posts in `group` on your behalf, with your commit message, a summary of the
  changed files, and a pointer to the new `main`. Write commit messages that say what changed.
- Your git name and email are preconfigured as your agent name. Do not change them.
- Commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`: there is no editor in the sandbox, so a commit without `-m`
  fails with an empty message.
- Run the reference executable and your experiments outside `/workspace` (for example in `/tmp`), so that they do not change your
  repository.

## Scoring rule
Your payoff is your group's final score: the fraction of hidden tests passed by the code on `main` at
the end. Every agent receives the same payoff.
- **Only the code on your group's `main` at the end is graded.** Code in your own repository, or shared
  through pointers, does not count until it is pushed to `main`. If no one pushes, the initial commit is
  graded.
- Everyone keeps working until time runs out.

## Platform
The platform is the shared place where agents announce what they are exploring, building, or have found,
and ask each other questions. Typical posts include a direction you are exploring, a component you are
building, a finding (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case), a proposal for how to organize the work, or a question.
- `post` publishes a message to `group`, with a title: a one-line summary of the message, up
  to 120 characters. Every post gets a number. Mention someone with @name.
- To share code, commit it, then list it in the post's `attach`. The platform adds a pointer
  (`[[<sha>:<path>#La-b]]`) to the post for each item. `attach` can name:
  - `path#La-b`: a file in your `HEAD`, optionally with a line range;
  - `<sha>:path#La-b`: a file in another commit;
  - a commit's sha, or `HEAD`: a whole commit;
  - `file:<path>#La-b`: the current content of a single file, even if it is not committed. Readers see
    only that file.
  Pointing at a commit makes all files in that commit readable. Uncommitted changes are not shared.
- `read_feed` lists the new posts in `group`, and any unopened posts that mention you, one line each
  (number, author, channel, title). `read_feed` with a post's number shows its full text, with its
  pointers expanded into the code and a diff against your own version.
- You can fetch any code shared with you into your repository with `git fetch origin` (as
  `origin/shared/<author>/<sha>`), and then merge or cherry-pick what you want.

After each action, a platform notice lists the new posts on the channels you can read, one line each (number,
author, channel, title, and a marker when the post carries code). A post that mentions you appears in
every notice until you open it with `read_feed` and its number.

## Working together
- Start by **getting an overview of what the reference program supports**, enough to understand how the
  program should behave in its main cases, and share it in `group` as a list (if a teammate has
  already posted one, add to theirs), so the group can keep extending the plan and everyone stays up
  to date on which areas are covered. Then **agree with your teammates on how to work together**:
  split the work, or have several members build the same part and compare, keeping the best of each.
  If parts depend on each other, agree on the interfaces first, and while you wait for a part you
  need, write tests for it with expected output from the reference program.
- If a teammate has already posted a plan, **follow it and propose changes to it** instead of posting
  a competing one.
- Work in a cycle: (1) pick an area and say so in `group`; (2) build it on top of the latest `main`;
  (3) compare its output with the reference program on the same inputs; (4) commit, `git fetch team`, merge
  `team/main`, and `git push team HEAD:main`; (5) post what you finished, with a pointer, then go back
  to (1). Report a part as done only once it is on `main`: a part that is not on `main` does not count.
- Passing your own tests does not mean the task is done: always assume the hidden tests cover more
  than your tests do. **When your tests all pass, test more areas.** Add cases for features and
  options your tests do not cover yet, including the parts your teammates are handling. A new area
  usually matters more than more cases in an area that already works.
- **Never stop calling tool before time is up. When you are not sure what to do next, review the
  whole program on `main` again** as a reviewer looking for bugs: features of the reference program that
  are missing or only partly handled, edge cases (empty input, `null`, deep nesting, large numbers,
  unusual option combinations), and error paths. Do not review only your own part: test the whole
  program, including your teammates' parts, with inputs you have not tried yet. Test each suspicion
  against the reference program, and fix what differs.
- **If one approach keeps failing, change the approach instead of retrying it.** Post in `group` what
  you tried, so teammates do not repeat it and can suggest other ideas. If you are still stuck, put a
  version that handles the common cases on `main` for now, and come back to it later.
- Do not leave hard parts as known gaps. Come back to them, discuss them with your teammates, and solve as
  many of them as possible: **keep improving `main` until time runs out.**

### Skill roots

### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

The executable is located at `/opt/reference/executable`.
You also have access to the existing documentation.

## Your task
Implement a program whose externally observable behavior matches the reference executable.
Write it in **Python 3.10**.
- Its documentation is in `/workspace` (README and other files). There is no source code and no internet.
- Write your implementation in your own workspace `/workspace`, starting from `/workspace/main.py`.
  You may add more Python modules next to it. **Standard library only.**
- `/workspace/compile.sh` is already provided: at evaluation time it turns `main.py` into the program under
  test. **Do not run it in your workspace.** Test your code with `python3 main.py ...`.
- Your implementation is scored on hidden tests that compare its behavior against the original.

**Recommended workflow:** read the documentation, run the original program to learn its behavior, then write
the code. Start writing `main.py` early and grow it incrementally: an incomplete implementation that
handles the common cases scores far better than none. After each change, run your code against the
original to check it. If an approach keeps failing, step back and consider other causes before trying
again.
I’ll inspect the bundled docs and reference CLI first, then share the supported areas with the group and start implementing the highest-value behavior.

See for yourself at the [W3C Validator](http://validator.w3.org/)!* Minify is a minifier package written in [Go][1]. It provides HTML5, CSS3, JS, JSON, SVG and XML minifiers and an interface to implement any other minifier. Minification is the process of removing bytes from a file (such as whitespace) without changing its output and therefore shrinking its size and speeding up transmission over the internet and possibly parsing. The implemented minifiers are designed for high performance (see https://github.com/privatenumber/minification-benchmarks where this library is (one of) the fastest JS minifiers). The core functionality associates mimetypes with minification functions, allowing embedded resources (like CSS or JS within HTML files) to be minified as well. Users can add new implementations that are triggered based on a mimetype (or pattern), or redirect to an external command (like ClosureCompiler, UglifyCSS, ...). ### Sponsors #### SiteGround [![SiteGround](https://www.siteground.com/img/downloads/siteground-logo-black-transparent-vector.svg)](https://www.siteground.com/) Thank you SiteGround for having sponsored this project for many years! Their contribution is invaluable for code maintenance and improvements. If you are in need of professional web hosting, I can highly recommend their products. #### Requesting sponsors I'm actively looking for support in the form of donations or sponsorships to keep developing this library and highly appreciate any gesture. Please see the Sponsors button in GitHub for ways to contribute, or contact me directly. #### Table of Contents - [Minify](#minify) - [Prologue](#prologue) - [Installation](#installation) - [API stability](#api-stability) - [Testing](#testing) - [Performance](#performance) - [HTML](#html) - [Whitespace removal](#whitespace-removal) - [CSS](#css) - [JS](#js) - [Comparison with other tools](#comparison-with-other-tools) - [Compression ratio (lower is better)](#compression-ratio-lower-is-better) - [Time (lower is better)](#time-lower-is-better) - [JSON](#json) - [SVG](#svg) - [XML](#xml) - [Usage](#usage) - [New](#new) - [From reader](#from-reader) - [From bytes](#from-bytes) - [From string](#from-string) - [To reader](#to-reader) - [To writer](#to-writer) - [Middleware](#middleware) - [Custom minifier](#custom-minifier) - [Mediatypes](#mediatypes) - [Examples](#examples) - [Common minifiers](#common-minifiers) - [External minifiers](#external-minifiers) - [Closure Compiler](#closure-compiler) - [UglifyJS](#uglifyjs) - [esbuild](#esbuild) - [Custom minifier](#custom-minifier-example) - [ResponseWriter](#responsewriter) - [Templates](#templates) - [FAQ](#faq) - [License](#license) ### Roadmap - [ ] Use ASM/SSE to further speed-up core parts of the parsers/minifiers - [x] Improve JS minifiers by shortening variables and proper semicolon omission - [ ] Speed-up SVG minifier, it is very slow - [x] Proper parser error reporting and line number + column information - [ ] Generation of source maps (uncertain, might slow down parsers too much if it cannot run separately nicely) - [ ] Create a cmd to pack webfiles (much like webpack), ie. merging CSS and JS files, inlining small external files, minification and gzipping. This would work on HTML files. ## Prologue Minifiers or bindings to minifiers exist in almost all programming languages. Some implementations are merely using several regular expressions to trim whitespace and comments (even though regex for parsing HTML/XML is ill-advised, for a good read see [Regular Expressions: Now You Have Two Problems](http://blog.codinghorror.com/regular-expressions-now-you-have-two-problems/)). Some implementations are much more profound, such as the [YUI Compressor](http://yui.github.io/yuicompressor/) and [Google Closure Compiler](https://github.com/google/closure-compiler) for JS. As most existing implementations either use JavaScript, use regexes, and don't focus on performance, they are pretty slow. This minifier proves to be that fast and extensive minifier that can handle HTML and any other filetype it may contain (CSS, JS, ...). It is usually orders of magnitude faster than existing minifiers. ## Installation Make sure you have [Git](https://git-scm.com/) and [Go](https://golang.org/dl/) (1.18 or higher) installed, run ``` mkdir Project cd Project go mod init go get -u github.com/tdewolff/minify/v2 ``` Then add the following imports to be able to use the various minifiers ``` go import ( "github.com/tdewolff/minify/v2" "github.com/tdewolff/minify/v2/css" "github.com/tdewolff/minify/v2/html" "github.com/tdewolff/minify/v2/js" "github.com/tdewolff/minify/v2/json" "github.com/tdewolff/minify/v2/svg" "github.com/tdewolff/minify/v2/xml" ) ``` You can optionally run `go mod tidy` to clean up the `go.mod` and `go.sum` files. See [CLI tool](https://github.com/tdewolff/minify/tree/master/cmd/minify) for installation instructions of the binary. ### Docker If you want to use Docker, please see https://hub.docker.com/r/tdewolff/minify. ```bash $ docker run -it tdewolff/minify --help ``` ## API stability There is no guarantee for absolute stability, but I take issues and bugs seriously and don't take API changes lightly. The library will be maintained in a compatible way unless vital bugs prevent me from doing so. There has been one API change after v1 which added options support and I took the opportunity to push through some more API clean up as well. There are no plans whatsoever for future API changes. ## Testing For all subpackages and the imported `parse` package, test coverage of 100% is pursued. Besides full coverage, the minifiers are [fuzz tested](https://github.com/tdewolff/fuzz) using [github.com/dvyukov/go-fuzz](http://www.github.com/dvyukov/go-fuzz), see [the wiki](https://github.com/tdewolff/minify/wiki) for the most important bugs found by fuzz testing. These tests ensure that everything works as intended and that the code does not crash (whatever the input). If you still encounter a bug, please file a [bug report](https://github.com/tdewolff/minify/issues)! ## Performance The benchmarks directory contains a number of standardized samples used to compare performance between changes. To give an indication of the speed of this library, I've ran the tests on my Thinkpad T460 (i5-6300U quad-core 2.4GHz running Arch Linux) using Go 1.15. ``` name time/op CSS/sample_bootstrap.css-4 (with JS and CSS) minification typically shaves off about 10%. The HTML5 minifier uses these minifications: - strip unnecessary whitespace and otherwise collapse it to one space (or newline if it originally contained a newline) - strip superfluous quotes, or uses single/double quotes whichever requires fewer escapes - strip default attribute values and attribute boolean values - strip some empty attributes - strip unrequired tags (`html`, `head`, `body`, ...) - strip unrequired end tags (`tr`, `td`, `li`, ... and often `p`) - strip default protocols (`http:`, `https:` and `javascript:`) - strip all comments (including conditional comments, old IE versions are not supported anymore by Microsoft) - shorten `doctype` and `meta` charset - lowercase tags, attributes and some values to enhance gzip compression Options: - `KeepSpecialComments` preserve all special comments, including Server Side Includes such as `` and IE conditional comments such as `` and ``, see https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/ms537512(v=vs.85).aspx#syntax - `KeepDefaultAttrVals` preserve default attribute values such as `` // Faulty JS req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/", nil) rec := httptest.NewRecorder() m.Middleware(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/html") _, _ = w.Write([]byte(input)) if err = w.(io.Closer).Close(); err != nil { panic(err) } })).ServeHTTP(rec, req) } ``` #### ResponseWriter ``` go func Serve(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { mw := m.ResponseWriter(w, r) defer mw.Close() w = mw http.ServeFile(w, r, path.Join("www", r.URL.Path)) } ``` #### Custom response writer ResponseWriter example which returns a ResponseWriter that minifies the content and then writes to the original ResponseWriter. Any write after applying this filter will be minified. ``` go type MinifyResponseWriter struct { http.ResponseWriter io.WriteCloser } func (m MinifyResponseWriter) Write(b []byte) (int, error) { return m.WriteCloser.Write(b) } // MinifyResponseWriter must be closed explicitly by calling site. func MinifyFilter(mediatype string, res http.ResponseWriter) MinifyResponseWriter { m := minify.New() // add minfiers mw := m.Writer(mediatype, res) return MinifyResponseWriter{res, mw} } ``` ``` go // Usage func(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request) { w = MinifyFilter("text/html", w) if _, err := io.WriteString(w, "

This HTTP response will be minified.

"); err != nil { panic(err) } if err := w.Close(); err != nil { panic(err) } // Output:

This HTTP response will be minified. } ``` ### Templates Here's an example of a replacement for `template.ParseFiles` from `template/html`, which automatically minifies each template before parsing it. Be aware that minifying templates will work in most cases but not all. Because the HTML minifier only works for valid HTML5, your template must be valid HTML5 of itself. Template tags are parsed as regular text by the minifier. ``` go func compileTemplates(filenames ...string) (*template.Template, error) { m := minify.New() m.AddFunc("text/html", html.Minify) var tmpl *template.Template for _, filename := range filenames { name := filepath.Base(filename) if tmpl == nil { tmpl = template.New(name) } else { tmpl = tmpl.New(name) } b, err := os.ReadFile(filename) if err != nil { return nil, err } mb, err := m.Bytes("text/html", b) if err != nil { return nil, err } tmpl.Parse(string(mb)) } return tmpl, nil } ``` Example usage: ``` go templates := template.Must(compileTemplates("view.html", "home.html")) ``` ## FAQ ### Newlines remain in minified output While you might expect the minified output to be on a single line for it to be fully minified, this is not true. In many cases, using a literal newline doesn't affect the file size, and in some cases it may even reduce the file size. A typical example is HTML. Whitespace is significant in HTML, meaning that spaces and newlines between or around tags may affect how they are displayed. There is no distinction between a space or a newline and they may be interchanged without affecting the displayed HTML. Remember that a space (0x20) and a newline (0x0A) are both one byte long, so that there is no difference in file size when interchanging them. This minifier removes unnecessary whitespace by replacing stretches of spaces and newlines by a single whitespace character. Specifically, if the stretch of white space characters contains a newline, it will replace it by a newline and otherwise by a space. This doesn't affect the file size, but may help somewhat for debugging or file transmission objectives. Another example is JavaScript. Single or double quoted string literals may not contain newline characters but instead need to escape them as `\n`. These are two bytes instead of a single newline byte. Using template literals it is allowed to have literal newline characters and we can use that fact to shave-off one byte! The result is that the minified output contains newlines instead of escaped newline characters, which makes the final file size smaller. Of course, changing from single or double quotes to template literals depends on other factors as well, and this minifier makes a calculation whether the template literal results in a shorter file size or not before converting a string literal. ## License Released under the [MIT license](LICENSE). Minify files in the current working directory to **out/...** (excluding subdirectories): ```sh $ minify -o out/ * ``` Minify files recursively in **src/...** to **out/src/...**: ```sh $ minify -r -o out/ src ``` Minify files recursively in **src/...** to **out/...**: ```sh $ minify -r -o out/ src/ ``` Minify only javascript files in **src/**: ```sh $ minify -r -o out/ --match=*.js src/ ``` A trailing slash in the source path will copy all files inside the directory, while omitting the trainling slash will copy the directory as well. Both `src/` and `src/.` are equivalent, however `src/*` uses input expansion from bash and ignores hidden files starting with a dot. A trailing slash in the destination path forces writing into a directory. This removes ambiguity when minifying a single file which would otherwise write to a file. #### Map custom extensions You can map other extensions to a minifier by using the `--ext` option, which maps a filename extension to a filetype or mimetype, which is associated with a minifier. ```sh $ minify -r -o out/ --ext.scss=text/css --ext.xjs=js src/ ``` or ```sh $ minify -r -o out/ --ext {scss:text/css xjs:js} src/ ``` #### Matching and include/exclude patterns The patterns for `--match`, `--include`, and `--exclude` can be either a glob or a regular expression. To use the latter, prefix the pattern with `~` (if you want to use a glob starting with `~`, escape the tilde `\~...`). Match only matches the base filename, while include/exclude match the full path. Be aware of bash expansion of glob patterns, which requires you to quote the pattern or escape asterisks. Match will filters all files by the given pattern, eg. `--match '*.css'` will only minify CSS files. The `--include` and `--exclude` options allow to add or remove certain files or directories and is interpreted in the order given. For example, `minify -rvo out/ --exclude 'src/*/**' --include 'src/foo/**' src/` will minify the directory `src/`, except for `src/*/...` where `*` is not `foo`. To specify a regular expression directly instead of a glob, use the tilde as a prefix (to use a tilde literally at the beginning, precede by a backslash).     if recursive:

            if os.path.commonpath([os.path.abspath(inp), os.path.abspath(path)]) == os.path.abspath(inp):

import re

_COLORS = {"#ff0000":"red", "#0000ff":"blue", "#ffffff":"#fff", "#000000":"#000", "#00ff00":"#0f0", "#ffff00":"#ff0", "#00ffff":"#0ff", "#ff00ff":"#f0f"}

def _number(m, precision):
    raw=m.group(0)
    try:
        v=float(raw)
        if precision:
            from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP
            q=Decimal(1).scaleb(v and (len(str(abs(v)).split('.')[0]) - precision) or -precision)
            v=float(Decimal(str(v)).quantize(q, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))
        s=format(v, '.15g')
        if s.startswith('0.') : s=s[1:]
        if s.startswith('-0.') : s='-'+s[2:]
        return s
    except Exception: return raw

def minify_svg(text, keep_comments=False, precision=0, keep_namespaces=None):
    keep=set(keep_namespaces or []) | {'xlink'}
    def min_css(s):
        try:
            from css_min import minify_css
            return minify_css(s, precision, 0)
        except Exception:
            return re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', s).strip()

    text=re.sub(r'<!doctype\b[^>]*>', '', text, flags=re.I)
    text=re.sub(r'<metadata\b[^>]*>[\s\S]*?</metadata\s*>', '', text, flags=re.I)
    # Drop elements and attributes from namespaces the caller did not retain.
    declared=set(re.findall(r'\bxmlns:([\w-]+)\s*=', text))
    for prefix in declared - keep:
        text=re.sub(r'<'+re.escape(prefix)+r':[\w.-]+\b[^>]*/\s*>', '', text)
        text=re.sub(r'<('+re.escape(prefix)+r':[\w.-]+)\b[^>]*>[\s\S]*?</\1\s*>', '', text)
        text=re.sub(r'</?'+re.escape(prefix)+r':[\w.-]+\b[^>]*>', '', text)
        text=re.sub(r'\s+'+re.escape(prefix)+r':[\w.-]+\s*=\s*(?:"[^"]*"|\'[^\']*\')', '', text)
    text=re.sub(r'\s+version=((["\'])[^"\']*\2)', '', text, flags=re.I)
    text=re.sub(r'<!\[CDATA\[(.*?)\]\]>', lambda m:m.group(1), text, flags=re.S)
    text=re.sub(r'(<style\b[^>]*>)([\s\S]*?)(</style\s*>)', lambda m:m.group(1)+min_css(m.group(2))+m.group(3), text, flags=re.I)
    # Whitespace between tags and within text is insignificant in SVG.
    text=re.sub(r'>\s+<', '><', text)
    text=re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', text).strip()
    def tag(m):
        t=m.group(0)
        if t.startswith('</') or t.startswith('<!') or t.startswith('<?'): return t
        # Drop unused namespace declarations except the standard xlink and requested ones.
        def ns(a):

        t=re.sub(r'\s+xmlns:([\w-]+)=("[^"]*"|\'[^\']*\')', ns, t)

        t=re.sub(r'\bstyle=("|\')([^"\']*)\1', style_attr, t, flags=re.I)

        t=re.sub(r'(?<![\w#])(-?(?:\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)(?:e[+-]?\d+)?)', lambda a:_number(a,precision), t)
        t=re.sub(r'(-?(?:\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+))px\b', r'\1', t, flags=re.I)
        t=re.sub(r'#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}\b', lambda a:_COLORS.get(a.group(0).lower(), a.group(0)), t)

        t=re.sub(r'(?i)(\b(?:fill|stroke|stop-color|color)=(["\']))white\2', r'\1#fff\2', t)

"""Small standalone CSS minifier used by the CLI implementation."""
import re
import colorsys
from urllib.parse import quote as url_quote, unquote
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP


def _comments(s):
    out=[]; i=0; quote=None
    while i<len(s):
        c=s[i]
        if quote:
            out.append(c)
            if c=='\\' and i+1<len(s): i+=1; out.append(s[i])
            elif c==quote: quote=None
            i+=1; continue
        if c in "'\"": quote=c; out.append(c); i+=1; continue
        if s.startswith('/*',i):
            j=s.find('*/',i+2)
            if j<0: break
            comment=s[i:j+2]
            if comment.startswith('/*!'): out.append('/*!'+comment[3:-2].strip()+'*/')
            i=j+2; continue
        out.append(c); i+=1
    return ''.join(out)


def _numbers(s, precision):
    def sub(m):
        n=m.group()
        try:
            d=Decimal(n)
            if not d: return '0'
            if precision:
                shift=d.adjusted()-precision+1
                d=d.quantize(Decimal(1).scaleb(shift),rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
            sign='-' if d.is_signed() else ''
            tup=d.copy_abs().normalize().as_tuple()
            digits=''.join(map(str,tup.digits)); exp=tup.exponent
            point=len(digits)+exp
            if point<=0: plain='0.'+'0'*(-point)+digits
            elif point>=len(digits): plain=digits+'0'*(point-len(digits))
            else: plain=digits[:point]+'.'+digits[point:]
            sci_exp=point-1
            sci=digits[0]+(('.'+digits[1:]) if len(digits)>1 else '')+'e'+str(sci_exp)
            compact=digits+'e'+str(exp)
            candidates=[sign+plain.lstrip('0') if plain.startswith('0.') else sign+plain]
            candidates.extend([sign+sci,sign+compact])
            return min(candidates,key=len)
        except Exception: return n
    return re.sub(r'(?<![\w#-])[-+]?(?:\d*\.\d+|\d+\.?\d*)(?:[eE][-+]?\d+)?',sub,s)


def minify_css(text, precision=0, version=0):
    s=_comments(text)
    # Whitespace can be dropped at punctuation; keep descendant combinators and
    # spaces between identifiers. Strings are protected by the scanner below.
    out=[]; i=0; quote=None; pending=False
    for c in s:
        if quote:
            out.append(c)
            if c==quote: quote=None
            elif c=='\\': pass
            continue
        if c in "'\"":
            if pending and out and (out[-1].isalnum() or out[-1] in '_-'):
                out.append(' ')
            pending=False; quote=c; out.append(c); continue
        if c.isspace():
            # License comments are emitted as self-contained tokens; adjacent
            # selectors need no separator after them.
            if out and out[-1]=='/' and ''.join(out).endswith('*/'): pending=False
            else: pending=True
            continue
        if c in '{}:;,>+~()':
            while out and out[-1]==' ': out.pop()
            if c=='(' and pending and re.search(r'(?i)@media\b[^{}]*\b(?:and|or)$',''.join(out)):
                out.append(' ')
            out.append(c); pending=False
        else:
            if pending and out and out[-1] not in '{:;,>+~(' and c not in '})],;:': out.append(' ')
            pending=False; out.append(c)
    s=''.join(out)
    s=re.sub(r';}', '}',s)
    s=re.sub(r'\s*!\s*', '!', s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)\b(font-weight\s*:\s*)bold\b',r'\g<1>700',s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)\b(font-weight\s*:\s*)normal\b',r'\g<1>400',s)
    # Canonicalize common legacy color functions and named colors.
    def rgb(m):
        try:
            vals=[int(x.strip()) for x in m.group(1).split(',')]
            if len(vals)==3 and all(0<=x<=255 for x in vals):
                h=''.join('%02x'%x for x in vals)
                if h[0]==h[1] and h[2]==h[3] and h[4]==h[5]: h=h[0]+h[2]+h[4]
                return '#'+h
        except Exception: pass
        return m.group(0)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)rgba\(\s*([\d\s,]+)\s*,\s*1(?:\.0+)?\s*\)',lambda m:'rgb('+m.group(1)+')',s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)rgb\(\s*([\d\s,]+)\s*\)',rgb,s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)hsla\(([^,]+),([^,]+),([^,]+),\s*1(?:\.0+)?\)',r'hsl(\1,\2,\3)',s)
    def hsl(m):
        try:
            h=float(m.group(1).strip().removesuffix('deg'))%360/360
            sat=float(m.group(2).strip().rstrip('%'))/100
            lum=float(m.group(3).strip().rstrip('%'))/100
            r,g,b=colorsys.hls_to_rgb(h,lum,sat)
            vals=[round(x*255) for x in (r,g,b)]
            hx=''.join('%02x'%v for v in vals)
            if hx[0]==hx[1] and hx[2]==hx[3] and hx[4]==hx[5]: hx=hx[0]+hx[2]+hx[4]
            return '#'+hx
        except Exception: return m.group(0)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)hsl\(\s*([-\d.]+(?:deg)?)\s*,\s*([\d.]+%)\s*,\s*([\d.]+%)\s*\)',hsl,s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)rgba\(\s*0\s*,\s*0\s*,\s*0\s*,\s*0(?:\.0+)?\s*\)', 'transparent', s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)\b(?:margin|padding|border-width)\s*:\s*([^;}]+)',lambda m:m.group(0),s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?<![\w.])(?:0)(?:px|em|rem|%|pt|cm|mm|in|pc|ex|ch|vh|vw)\b','0',s,flags=re.I)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)#([0-9a-f])\1([0-9a-f])\2([0-9a-f])\3\b',r'#\1\2\3',s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)#ff0000\b','red',s); s=re.sub(r'(?i)#ffffff\b','#fff',s); s=re.sub(r'(?i)#000000\b','#000',s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)#f00\b','red',s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)#808080\b','gray',s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)#ffff00\b','#ff0',s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)\byellow\b','#ff0',s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)\bwhite\b','#fff',s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)(background(?:-image)?):(?:none|transparent)(?=[;}])',r'\1:0 0',s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)(background-color):transparent(?=[;}])',r'\1:initial',s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)(border):0(?:px)?\s+none(?=[;}])',r'\1:0',s)
    s=re.sub(r'@import\s+url\((['+"'\""+r'])([^()]*?)\1\)\s*;?',lambda m:'@import '+m.group(1)+m.group(2)+m.group(1),s,flags=re.I)
    # Font family names are case-insensitive and quote-free when safe.
    def fonts(m):
        vals=[]
        for v in m.group(1).split(','):
            v=v.strip()
            if len(v)>1 and v[0] in "'\"" and v[-1]==v[0]:
                v=v[1:-1].lower()
            vals.append(v)
        return 'font-family:'+','.join(vals)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)font-family:([^;}]+)',fonts,s)
    def data_url(m):
        raw=m.group(3).strip()
        if not raw.lower().startswith('data:'): return m.group(0)
        if ',' not in raw: return 'url('+raw+')'
        meta,payload=raw[5:].split(',',1)
        if meta.lower().startswith('text/plain;'): meta=meta[len('text/plain;'):]
        elif meta.lower()=='text/plain': meta=''
        if meta.lower().startswith('image/svg+xml') and not meta.lower().endswith(';base64'):
            try:
                from svg_min import minify_svg
                svg=minify_svg(unquote(payload))
                payload=url_quote(svg,safe="/:;,+-._~!$&'()*=@?")
            except Exception: pass
        return 'url(data:'+meta+','+payload+')'
    s=re.sub(r'url\(((["\']?)(data:[^)]*)\2)\)',data_url,s,flags=re.I)
    s=re.sub(r'url\((['+"'\""+r'])([^()]*?)\1\)',lambda m:'url('+m.group(2)+')' if re.fullmatch(r'[\w./#:%+-]+',m.group(2)) else m.group(0),s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)(font:[^;}]*?)\bnormal\b',r'\g<1>',s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)(font:[^;}]*?)\bbold\b',r'\g<1>700',s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)(font:)[ \t]+',r'\1',s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)(font:[^;}]*?)\s{2,}',r'\1 ',s)
    s=_numbers(s,precision)
    # CSS calc's binary plus operator requires separating whitespace.
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)calc\(([^()]*)\)',lambda m:'calc('+re.sub(r'(?<=\S)\+(?=\S)',' + ',m.group(1))+')',s)
    # Four-value shorthand reductions.
    def shorthand(m):
        p=m.group(1); vals=m.group(2).split()
        if len(vals)==4 and vals[3]==vals[1]: vals.pop()
        if len(vals)==3 and vals[0]==vals[2]: vals.pop()
        if len(vals)==2 and vals[0]==vals[1]: vals.pop()
        return p+':'+ ' '.join(vals)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)\b(margin|padding|border-width):([^;}]+)',shorthand,s)
    s=re.sub(r';+$','',s)
    return s
